title: The Three Billy Goats Gruff
summary: Three billy goats named Gruff want to cross the bridge to the green hillside, but under the bridge lives a hungry troll. A classic Norwegian folktale about cleverness, courage and a lot of "tip-tap" on the bridge.
pages:
Once upon a time there were three billy goats who wanted to go up to the hillside to eat grass and get fat.
And all three of them had the same name: Gruff.

On the way to the hillside there was a bridge over a stream, and they had to cross it.
And under the bridge lived a big, ugly troll, with eyes as big as plates and a nose as long as a pole.

First came the littlest billy goat to cross the bridge.
"Tip-tap, tip-tap!" went the bridge.
"Who's that tip-tapping over my bridge?" roared the troll.

"Oh! It's only me, the littlest Billy Goat Gruff. I'm going up to the hillside to get fat," said the billy goat in a tiny, tiny voice.
"Now I'm coming to gobble you up!" said the troll.

"Oh, no! Please don't take me. I'm too little," said the billy goat. "Wait a bit until the second Billy Goat Gruff comes. He's much bigger."
"Oh, all right! Be off with you," said the troll.

A little while later, the second Billy Goat Gruff came to cross the bridge.
"Tip-tap! Tip-tap! Tip-tap!" went the bridge.
"Who's that tip-tapping over my bridge?" roared the troll.

"Oh! It's the second Billy Goat Gruff, and I'm going up to the hillside to get fat," said the billy goat, whose voice wasn't quite so small.
"Now I'm coming to gobble you up!" said the troll.

"Oh, no! Don't take me. Wait a bit until the big Billy Goat Gruff comes. He's much, much bigger."
"Very well! Be off with you," said the troll.

And just then along came the big Billy Goat Gruff.
"TRIP-TRAP! TRIP-TRAP! TRIP-TRAP!" went the bridge, for the billy goat was so heavy that the bridge creaked and groaned under him.

"Who's that stomping over my bridge?" roared the troll.
"It's me! The BIG Billy Goat Gruff!" said the billy goat in a deep, gruff voice.
"Now I'm coming to gobble you up!" roared the troll.

"Well, come along, then! I've got two horns so sharp and so strong,
I'll toss you away past the hills before long!
And I've got four hooves just as heavy as stones,
I'll scatter you into little bits and bones!"
That's what the big billy goat said. He charged at the troll, butted him with his horns, and tossed him high, high up, right into the stream.

And after that he went up to the hillside too. There the billy goats got so fat that they could hardly walk back home. And if the fat hasn't come off them yet, they're fat to this very day.
And so,
"Snip, snap, snout,
this tale's told out!"
